topic: Computer Architecture, CPU, ALU and CU
description: Computer Architecture defines the internal design and functioning of a computer. It includes the Central Processing Unit (CPU), Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), and Control Unit (CU), which are primarily responsible for data processing and system control. This is a crucial topic for competitive exams in the Computer Knowledge section.

sections.title: Fundamentals of Computer Architecture
sections.description: The basic design model of a computer and the communication pathways between its primary components.

key_concepts.explanation: A computer design model where both data and instructions are stored in the same memory space. It is also known as the 'Stored Program Concept'.
A conceptual group of wires that transfers data, memory addresses, and control signals between the CPU, main memory, and Input/Output (I/O) devices.

historical_events.significance: Proposed by the great mathematician John von Neumann, this architectural model forms the foundational basis of almost all modern computers today.

important_facts.fact: The System Bus is broadly classified into three main types: Data Bus, Address Bus, and Control Bus.

sections.title: Central Processing Unit (CPU)
sections.description: The primary component of a computer that acts as its 'brain' and processes all programmatic instructions.

key_concepts.explanation: Referred to as the brain of the computer. It fetches, decodes, and executes all instructions received from hardware and software.
A single Integrated Circuit (IC) silicon chip that contains the entire Central Processing Unit.

key_associations.extra_info: The processing speed of modern computers is usually measured in Gigahertz (GHz).
Examples include Dual-core (2), Quad-core (4), and Octa-core (8) processors.

important_facts.fact: The world's first commercial microprocessor was the 'Intel 4004', developed and released in 1971.
India's first indigenous microprocessor is 'Shakti', developed by the researchers at IIT Madras.

sections.title: Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)
sections.description: The digital circuit within the CPU that handles all mathematical calculations and logical decisions.

key_concepts.explanation: A critical component of the CPU that is strictly dedicated to executing all arithmetic (mathematical) and logical (decision-making) operations.
Performing basic mathematical tasks like addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division on data.
Comparing data values (such as determining greater than, less than, or equal to) and performing Boolean operations like AND, OR, and NOT.

important_facts.fact: The ALU solves highly complex calculations by breaking them down into simpler, sequential arithmetic and logical steps.

sections.title: Control Unit (CU)
sections.description: The component that directs, manages, and coordinates all operations within the computer system.

key_concepts.explanation: Often referred to as the nervous system of the computer. It directs the memory, ALU, and input/output devices on how to respond to program instructions.
The four fundamental steps adopted by the CU to process an instruction: Fetch (get instruction), Decode (translate), Execute (perform action), and Store (save result).

key_associations.extra_info: It converts program instructions into binary machine language so the ALU can understand and execute them.

important_facts.fact: The Control Unit does not process any actual data itself; rather, it only acts as a traffic manager coordinating the data flow across the system.

sections.title: Registers
sections.description: Extremely high-speed temporary memory locations embedded directly inside the CPU.

key_concepts.explanation: These are very small but the fastest memory units located within the CPU. They are used to temporarily store data, addresses, and instructions that are immediately needed for processing.

key_associations.extra_info: It specifically stores the intermediate mathematical and logical results of the operations performed by the ALU.
A crucial register that stores the memory address of the very next instruction to be fetched and executed.
It temporarily holds the specific instruction that is currently being decoded and executed by the CPU.

important_facts.fact: In the computer memory hierarchy, Registers possess the absolute highest read/write speed but the lowest storage capacity.
